_numbering_note: catalog_number pending the base/hybrid renumbering (see gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md); csv_id is the authoritative key for now.
sub_palette: near_eastern (akkadian) backbone + mesoamerican (mayan) substrate (cross-family fusion, Mesopotamian-leaning)

blend.backbone: near_eastern (akkadian: the alu/bit river-cities, the sangu temple-priesthood, construct-chain toponyms, emphatic gutturals and sh/q, -u/-tu/-um endings, SOV agglutinative grammar, penultimate stress)
blend.overlay: mesoamerican (mayan: the jungle k'uhul-kah of pyramid-acropolis and stela, the witz altar-mountain, glottalized stops, the Long-Count calendar and vigesimal count, jade/cacao/maize wealth)
blend.lean: Mesopotamian-heavy - the Akkadian temple-and-stele register dominates (rule, kin, temple, the great-river plain), the Mayan jungle endures beneath it (the witz-pyramid, the rain-forest, the jade and maize): two stepped-tower civilizations grown into one, the ziggurat of the Two Rivers and the witz of the jungle as a single tongue.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_03 Shinarur (Mesopotamian) x BASE_10 (Mesoamerican). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Mesopotamian base = Civilized, Mesoamerican base = Civilized, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Tollanur is Civilized (feudal). Concept: Tollanur = an Akkadian-Mesoamerican fusion - two ziggurat/pyramid temple-civilizations merged into one, the stepped tower of Babel and the witz-pyramid of the jungle as a single people (a Tollan-flavored 'place of reeds and stepped towers'). Backbone = Akkadian (the prestige temple-and-stele register: the alu-cities, the bit-ili god-houses, the construct-chain toponyms, rule/kin/temple/land words); substrate = Mayan (the jungle land it grew in: the witz-pyramid, the rain-forest, jade/cacao/maize/obsidian, the material and staple words). Common-word lexicon and rank titles draw on the real Akkadian and Maya registers (allowed, catalog 5.3) but are FUSED to a single Akkadian-shaped tongue via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Akkadian reflexes PRIMARY per family_near_eastern/hammuran, Mayan morphs SECONDARY per family_mesoamerican theonym_sets.mayan), never real Mesopotamian or Maya gods. All three alignments (per the alignment pass - all human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are ENGLISH (no approved foreign term applies to a fused Akkadian-Maya register); the Akkadian conlang forms move to ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. Deities via the per-family morph method.

phonology.palette: Akkadian backbone - emphatic and guttural consonants (q, kh, h, ', sh, ts), triconsonantal roots, vowels a/i/u, -u/-tu/-um endings, penultimate stress, construct chains - meeting a Mayan overlay: glottalized stops (b'/t'/k'/tz'/ch'), x = sh, final glottal stop, the -kah/-witz/-tun/-ab endings, agentive aj-/ix-, vigesimal count. Per the CSV: glottal stops with guttural sounds; grammar SOV with vigesimal root patterns - the Akkadian agglutinative case-inflections carried over the Mayan glottal substrate. Theophoric on the Akkadian reflexes (Tullaru-, Urlandu-) with Mayan morph variants (Tulax-, Orlanab-, aj-/ix- prefixed).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC; Akkadian mimation -um and construct-chains meeting Mayan glottalization and the final glottal stop; Mayan glottalized stops resolve to Akkadian emphatics/plain stops (k'>q, t'>t, tz'>ts, ch'>sh, b'>b) and the -tl/vigesimal clusters break to CVC + -u/-um; penultimate stress throughout; Akkadian Bit-/Dur-/Kar- construct toponyms over Mayan Noh-/Chak-/-witz elements.

sound_changes: Mayan glottalized stops/ejectives -> Akkadian emphatics and plain stops: k'>q, t'>t, tz'>ts, ch'>sh, b'>b; Mayan x and Akkadian sh both held as sh
Mayan final glottal stop and vowel-length drop; Nahua-areal -tl clusters and Mayan vigesimal/-tun roots break to CVC and take an Akkadian -u/-um (or -tu) ending; roots become Akkadian-shaped
Akkadian penultimate stress on all words; Akkadian construct-chains, mimation -um and triconsonantal stems permitted
retain Akkadian q, kh, ' and the held sh; retain a Mayan signature in the kept witz-/kah-/k'uh- roots; very short roots take an Akkadian -u/-um
fusion_rules.source_tilt: jungle/pyramid/material/staple words from Mayan roots (the jungle substrate works the land - the witz, the rain-forest, jade/cacao/maize/obsidian); rule/kin-line/temple/land/abstract/quality words from Akkadian roots (the prestige stele-and-temple register); every root then filtered to one Akkadian-shaped phonology

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Mayan jungle/material/staple-roots + Akkadian rule/kin/temple/land-roots, all run through one Akkadian-shaped sound-law (Mayan glottals -> emphatics, vigesimal/-tun clusters fit to CVC + -u/-um, penultimate stress); portmanteaus mark the blended pyramid-institutions and bloodline. No slashes - one word per concept.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Akkadian populace keep the 'mar-' (son of) patronymic and theophoric constructs; the Mayan substrate keeps the shibal- (lineage, < ch'ib'al) house and the aj-/ix- (he-of/she-of) prefixes on day-and-power names; the throne fuses both - a sharru who also carries a Bit- house-name and a witz-dynastic count.
morphology.compounding_rule: Akkadian construct-chains (Bit-[god], Dur-[ruler], Kar-[god]) layered over Mayan quality+feature compounds (Noh-[feature], Chak-[feature], [color]-witz): the capital Tollanur (the reed-place of stepped towers), Dur-Sharru (king's-fort), Noh-Witzbitu (the great pyramid-temple-city).

title_ladder.government: feudal (an Akkadian temple-and-stele aristocracy grown together with the Mayan jungle city-states: the sharru and his rubu-kin at the crown, the shaknu-governors over the kahalu-cities, the witz-priesthood and the scribal ekallu beneath; the Mayan ajaw-nobility and sajal-governors fold into the same ladder)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Akkadian ladder, ascending, with the Mayan substrate co-titles folded beneath. Hazannu (mayor) barony; Massaru (warden) march; Shaknu (appointed governor) county over the Mayan sajal; Turtanu (commander-in-chief) duchy over the ajaw-nobility; Rubu (prince) principality echoing the k'uhul ajaw (holy lord); Sharru (king) kingdom over a Sharrutu, the Mayan kalomte' (overlord) folded under the crown; Shar-kishshati (king-of-the-totality) empire over the Kishshatu. The jungle cities keep their ajaw and sajal and their ah-k'in (sun-priest) beneath the Akkadian crown; the sangu (city-priest) and scribal shatammu stand outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Akkadian and Maya registers (allowed); DISPLAY titles are English.
title_ladder.heir: Mar-Sharri (son of the king; the crown prince; the baah-ch'ok, head-youth, of the witz-dynasty)

vassalage.fealty: Ade (Akkadian loyalty-oath) / Patan-t'an (Mayan oath of service)

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH. No approved commonly-known foreign term applies to this fused Akkadian-Maya register, so English display titles are used throughout. The *_native conlang forms (Akkadian, with Mayan co-titles) are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Akkadian register carries a theophoric given name + mar- patronymic; the Mayan substrate carries an aj-/ix- + day-and-power name + shibal- lineage; order given-first.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Akkadian temple-city stock keep theophoric names (X-iddina, Warad-X) on the morphed canon-stems; the Mayan jungle stock keep aj-/ix- day-and-power names (Aj-Tulax, Ix-Rialtaj) on the morphed Mayan stems.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Akkadian devotional constructs: Warad-Tullaru (servant of Tullaru), Tullaru-iddina (Tullaru-gave-me); Mayan devotional with aj-/ix-: Aj-Tulax, Ix-Orlanab, calendar-day-and-power names.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Akkadian reflexes PRIMARY (family_near_eastern / hammuran morphs: Tullaru-, Urlandu-, Numunu-), Mayan morphs SECONDARY (family_mesoamerican.json theonym_sets.mayan: Tulax, Orlanab, Numench, aj-/ix- prefixed), never real Mesopotamian or Maya gods. Same shared pantheon, two registers. All three alignments. The witz (pyramid) and the ziggurat are one altar; the Long-Count calendar and the law-stele bind the sharru and the ajaw alike to the powers.
religion.the_one: Itarnu (Akk; Maya Aj Ternaj) - the distant Ancient One, honored not petitioned

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Tullaru (Maya Tulax) - the sun and judgment
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Rialtu (Maya Ix Rialtaj) - the mother, mercy

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Itarnu, Tullaru the just, Urlandu of the sworn war, Rialtu the merciful - and names the Chaotic powers lemnu (evil) or demonizes the Mayan Marakab/Wakix/Lusankaan, warded; the law-stele and the Long-Count calendar bind alike
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the ancestral dead (the deified sharru-kin and the uchben, the Mayan forebears) and the city-spirits of the bit-ili and the day-lords; the great powers invoked at the witz-pyramid and the temple situationally
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon (Marakshu, Bakidu-lemnu, the war-fire), and names the Lawful powers - and Itarnu - as the tyrant-gods to be defied; the bloodletting-rite turned to dread ends.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as -lemnu (Akkadian evil) or demonized in the Mayan register, keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Marakshu the City-Burner (Maya Marakab the War-Fire); Vacidus -> Bakidu-lemnu the Unmaking (Maya Wakix the Devourer); Lusanto -> Lusankaan the Hoard-Serpent.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Bit-ili (Akkadian god-house) or the Quhnellu (the Mayan k'uh-nah god-house) atop the witz of [power]: 'the Bit-ili of Tullaru', 'the Witz of Tulax'.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified law-givers and sharru-kin inscribed on the stele, and the deified k'uhul ajaw ancestors (the uchben), honored at the ziggurat and the carved stela atop the witz.

holy_symbol_motifs.Tullaru: a winged sun-disc above the law-stele and the bloodletting-glyph
holy_symbol_motifs.Urlandu: an iron blade crossed with the obsidian war-club
holy_symbol_motifs.Gayandu: the alluvial maize-field beneath the stepped witz
